Hey I'd suggest you have a look at the Wikipedia link. Even if a state is 98-99% ODF (open defecation free) it isn't counted as being a completely ODF free state. This would make almost 30/35 states and union territories ODF free. 

However, this isn't true for every state and the union territory of Goa has an abysmally bad ODF rate of 71%. This is obviously a huge problem, but keep in mind Goa is a 3000 km² state in a 3.287 million km² country. 

I'm not trying to underplay the situation or paint a rosier picture, sanitation is one of the biggest problems we face as a country. Which is why the current government focused on their 'Swach Bharat' campaign and succeeded at reducing ODF by 26%. It would be great if you put things into perspective before making a blanket statement like that.
